candidates.name: Erebuni Fortress
candidates.content: The excavations, recreations and museum of the nearly 3,000-year-old fortress that established Yerevan. Fairly well- (and maybe the best-) preserved fortress of Urartian Period in Armenia.

candidates.name: Cascades, Sculpture Park and Cafesjian Museum
candidates.content: The Sculpture Park is a small green zone in the immediate North of the Opera. Sculptures from Botero and other artists of international fame decorate the park. The park is part of Cafesjian Museum - the Armenian version of Guggenh

candidates.name: The National Art Gallery
candidates.content: Founded in 1921, the Gallery preserves more than 42,000 works of Armenian and international fine art and decorative-applied arts. Its collections include masterpieces by world-renowned artists such as Hovhannes Aivazovsky, Vardges

candidates.name: History Museum of Armenia
candidates.content: A roundup of the nation's history from early settlements to the 20th century. Lots of archaeological exhibits and pieces of art give an impression of each period. If you would like to move along the timeline then start at the top

candidates.name: Cafesjian Museum of Modern Art
candidates.hours: Escalators gallery daily 08:00-20:00; special galleries Fri-Sun 10:00-20:00
candidates.content: A modern art museum, housing the collection of Gerard Cafesjian. It has Arshile Gorky, Andy Warhol, Marc Chagall and other big names on display. The collection is very rich in Glass Art, has many pieces of the Libenský-Brychtová c

candidates.name: The Yerevan History Museum
candidates.price: 400 dram. Tour in Russian, English, French, German 3,000 dram
candidates.content: Presents all periods of the life in Yerevan starting from paleolithic settlements (50,000 years) to modern days. Ancient maps and the pictures of the lost city, pre-Soviet Erivan, are of special interest. Lift and sloping floors f

candidates.name: Modern Art Museum of Yerevan
candidates.content: Houses quite a selection of contemporary art by mostly Armenian artists. On the opposite side of the street, there is the newly opened HayArt cultural center as well as the Eduard Isabekyan Gallery.

candidates.name: Erebuni Museum of History
candidates.price: 1,000 dram for museum and site; 500 dram for site only. Tour in foreign language 2,500 dram
candidates.content: The museum stands at the foot of the Arin Berd hill, on top of which the Urartian Fortress Erebouni has stood since 782 BCE. The City-Fortress was excavated, some parts of the structure were reinforced and restored, and the fortre

candidates.name: Parajanov Museum
candidates.content: The House-Museum of Sergei Parajanov, a famous Soviet film director. The museum is best known for special Parajanov collages and art that everybody loves and enjoys. It is equally highly appreciated by children, teenagers and the

candidates.name: Martiros Saryan House-Museum
candidates.price: 1,000 dram. Tour in Russian, English, French 2,500 dram
candidates.content: If you are a lover of bright colours and enjoy Impressionist art then the House Museum of Martiros Saryan is a place for you. It's a 3-floor structure, designed by the artist and built during his lifetime, both as his home and a h

candidates.name: Armenian Genocide Memorial (Genocide Museum & Tsitsernakaberd Monument)
candidates.content: An austere monument & museum commemorating the victims of the Armenian Genocide. The permanent collection documents the 19th C community, then its ruthless destruction circa 1915 at the hands of the Ottoman Empire.Tsitsernakaberd

candidates.name: Armenian Railways Museum
candidates.alt: Museum of Railway Transport of Armenia
candidates.content: Presents the history of the Armenian railway, from 1895. Exhibits are labelled in Armenian and Russian, but not English. Several large exhibits are in an adjacent garden, accessible from the museum. A steam locomotive and carriage

candidates.name: Katoghike
candidates.alt: Holy Mother of God Kathoghike Church, Սուրբ Աստվածածին Կաթողիկէ Եկեղեցի
candidates.content: A tiny structure constructed in typical Armenian style. Katoghike means "cathedral"; the reason for the incongruity is that the original 13th century church had a much larger basilica attached to it in the 17th century - but that

candidates.name: St Gregory the Illuminator Cathedral
candidates.content: Completed in 2001 to commemorate the 1700th anniversary of Armenia as a Christian nation. The holy relics of St Gregory the Armenian were given back to the Armenian Church by the Vatican in 2001 and placed in this cathedral. The b

candidates.name: Saint Sarkis Cathedral
candidates.content: From the Victory Bridge (or alternatively the Brandy Factory building) there is a beautiful view on the church and surroundings (structures of different shades constructed in immediate proximity to the church during the Soviet yea

candidates.name: St Astvatsatsin of Nork
candidates.alt: Holy Cross Church, Սուրբ Խաչ եկեղեցու
candidates.content: This is the replica of a beautiful 18th-century St Holy Mother of God (Sb Astvatsatsin in Armenian) church destroyed during the Soviet years of forced secularisation. Because of the sudden death of the benefactor the church comple

candidates.name: Republic Square
candidates.alt: Armenian: Հանրապետության Հրապարակ Russian: Площадь Республики
candidates.content: The city's main square is a grand example of Soviet public architecture. The early buildings (the Houses of Government, the Ministry of Communications and the Marriott Hotel) are Neo-Classical with Armenian hints. The later buildi

candidates.name: Mashtots avenue
candidates.content: It's the 8-lane highway of the city which somehow also accommodates a pedestrian zones on the sides (result of standard Soviet planning of main 'Prospekts'). It is overly noisy because of the heavy traffic (mostly unorganised publ

candidates.name: Aram Khachaturyan House Museum
candidates.content: The home of late composer Aram Khachaturyan (1903-1978) has been turned into a museum. Things like his manuscripts and piano are on display here, and the building also has a concert hall.

candidates.name: Eduard Isabekyan Gallery
candidates.content: Small but good art museum, commemorating the eponymous artist. Housed in an interesting round building in Brutalist style.

candidates.name: Yerevan City Hall
candidates.content: The city's administration is housed in this massive five-story building. Construction started during Soviet times, was halted in 1991 for over a decade and the building was finally completed in 2004. The Yerevan History Museum is

candidates.name: Katoghike Tsiranavor Church of Avan
candidates.alt: Ավանի Սուրբ Աստվածածին Կաթողիկե Եկեղեցի, Katoghike Tsiranavor church, later renamed Surp Hovhannes
candidates.content: This is the city's oldest surviving church, which was completed in the 6th century.

candidates.name: St John The Baptist Church
candidates.content: A church with three naves, built in 1710 and renovated and expanded in the 1980s.

candidates.name: Ervand Kochar Museum
candidates.content: Small museum dedicated to the eponymous sculptor and artist.

candidates.name: Northern Avenue
candidates.content: Impossible to miss, this pedestrian avenue was opened in 2008 connecting Opera with Republic Square, the two hubs of central Yerevan. It's a post-modern response to post-World War II Soviet Yerevan architecture. It is emerging as

candidates.name: Freedom (or Theatrical) Square
candidates.content: On the north the square is bordered by the Opera House, followed by a park with a lake and full of open air cafés on the east, and from south it borders the Northern Avenue

candidates.name: Matenadaran
candidates.content: Houses the world's largest collection of Armenian illuminated manuscripts, and one of the largest such collections of any kind in the world. A display room has a sampling of some of the finest works, and the additional cost of the

candidates.name: Blue Mosque
candidates.content: An 18th-century Shia Islamic Mosque, one of the few surviving structures of a once (before Soviet secularisation) prospering Muslim community of Yerevan.

candidates.name: Yerevan Water World
candidates.hours: 12:00–21:00, indoor water park "Aquatek" is open all year round without holidays
candidates.content: A water park popular with the locals in the summers, it consists of a big open-air water park and a much smaller indoor one. Anybody can cool down there as in total it offers 7 outdoor and 3 indoor pools. There are also wall-climb

candidates.name: Lover's Park
candidates.content: One of the oldest parks of Yerevan. Renovated in tradition of Japanese landscaping with Armenian spirit. It often hosts open air art exhibitions and concerts. It is best reached by metro, station 'Marshal Baghramian' - perhaps the

candidates.name: The Opera House
candidates.content: The building is perhaps modeled after SemperOper of Dresden, however it is supposed to be double as beautiful as the Yerevan building is two sided: One side (entrance from the Theatrical/Freedom square) is home to Opera and Ballet

candidates.name: Yerevan Zoo
candidates.price: Adult 800 dram, children 12-16 years - 500 dram, children 3-12 years - 300 dram
candidates.content: Zoo is home to about 3,000 animals mainly representing South Caucasus and Armenia: bears, goats, snakes, Armenian mouflon and black vultures. Also from other parts of the world: lions, tigers, hyenas and an Asian elephants. It was

candidates.name: Botanical garden of Yerevan
candidates.content: The collection includes more than 200 species of endemic, rare and declining plants. However, after the collapse of the Soviet Union due to insufficient funds the condition of the park started declining and now it needs a lot of i

candidates.name: Lyon Park
candidates.content: Surrounding the artificial Vardarvar Lake, this park was renamed Lyon Park to honor France's second city. Lyon is a friendship city of Yerevan and the French funded the renovation of the park in the early 2010s.

candidates.name: Arten Theatre
candidates.content: Independent chamber theatre founded in 2022, in a former House of Culture with about 50 seats. Performances, play readings, labs and lectures; the programme is on the website.

candidates.name: Yerevan Circus
candidates.content: A new circus building finished in 2018, on the place of a former one which was demolished in 2012. Opening of the circus was planned for 2020, postponed by the pandemic and as of 2024 it has still yet to open.

candidates.name: Hrazdan Gorge partying
candidates.content: Visit one of the themed restaurants in the Hrazdan Gorge to see the locals partying. The food does not tend to venture far from barbecue and crayfish, but it is usually good barbecue, and the prices range from very reasonable to t

candidates.name: Children's Railway Park
candidates.content: Miniature railway for children to ride in, established in 1937.

candidates.name: Circular park
candidates.content: Despite its name, the park's shape is semi-circular. You can see several monuments to important Armenian and Russian imperial figures here.

candidates.name: English park
candidates.content: One of Yerevan's oldest parks, though smaller in size than it once was. It is popular with couples for wedding photographs.

candidates.name: The Swan Lake park
candidates.content: ends with the popular statue of the composer Arno Babajanyan, which brings attention to his famous nose and long fingers. The Swan Lake park usually hosts various open air art exhibitions. Ice-skate with many locals at the Swan La

candidates.name: Tumanyan park
candidates.content: Part of the Tumo Centre for Creative Technologies.

candidates.name: Moscow theatre
candidates.content: Opened in 1936, with 4 theatre halls.

candidates.name: Sundukyan State Academic Theatre
candidates.content: The oldest modern theatre in Armenia, here you can see the most famous actors of the country perform.

candidates.name: Yerevan's Birthday
candidates.content: Yerevan's birthday is usually celebrated on the second Saturday of October. It's usually a huge event, with central Yerevan being pedestrian only: there are many stages all over the city for theatrical or music (usually thematic -

candidates.name: Catch a concert
candidates.content: on the Cascades or the Lover's Park, and an art exhibition at Swan Lake park or Lover's Park.

candidates.name: Spartak Stadium
candidates.content: This is a mixed-use sports & athletics stadium just south of city centre.

candidates.name: Opera park
candidates.content: Spend a late night at a café in the Opera park, and outside the Melody Café for some of the best people watching in Yerevan.

candidates.name: Calumet
candidates.content: Bohemian, friendly, alternative crowd. Insanely smokey (seriously). There is no outdoor section so if you're not a fan of cigarette smoke, it might not be the place for you. English speaking staff and solid drinks selection. A nic

candidates.name: Roza
candidates.content: Small bar with great ambiance in old Yerevan building, and fantastic drinks. Try the Tutovni house cocktail made with the famous local mulberry vodka.

candidates.name: In Vino
candidates.content: The first wine bar on Saryan Street, that led the transformation of the entire neighborhood is still popular.

candidates.name: Jack's Pub
candidates.content: Good spot for a drink, the bloody mary is legendary and the basil gin cocktail is great in the summer. You'll likely meet some repats here.

candidates.name: Kami Club
candidates.content: Live music on many nights.

candidates.name: Stop Club
candidates.content: Rock club. Live music on many nights.

candidates.name: Mirzoyan Library
candidates.content: Started out as a space in a traditional courtyard with a collection of photography books, it's now a café with very nice drinks and creative and excellent bites and sweets. Free wifi.

candidates.name: Tavern Yerevan
candidates.content: The place for traditional Armenian cuisine. You'll have to rub shoulders with an occasional government function, a wedding shower or a busful of tourists, but the food is the real thing. Do not be scared by the names of the dishes

candidates.name: Mer Taghe
candidates.content: A small lahmejun joint on Tumanyan, and their lahmejuns have a big following. If you have some extra time and want to splurge, try the manti dumplings or the norahars, a kind of regional lasagna.

candidates.name: Artashi Mot
candidates.content: Cheap shaurmas, soups and kebabs upstairs, fancier but still well priced sit-down restaurant underground. Great place to have BBQ and to meet your traditional fast food cravings. The fancier part is considered by many to be the fi

candidates.name: Grand Candy Ponchikanots
candidates.content: Ponchiks are a regional type of donut. Fried dough stuffed with a custard and topped with powdered sugar. Grand Candy took over the old space of a popular former Soviet "ponchikanots", or place of ponchiks and this is a popular sp

candidates.name: Anteb
candidates.content: A family-run cafe that serves a huge variety of kebabs in a very casual cafe-type setting. The Adana and Urfa are a bargain at about 800 dram each and the Iskender, though slightly more expensive for 3,000 dram (May 2015) rivals t

candidates.name: Lavash
candidates.content: Very good menu of traditional Armenian cuisine. The large room upstairs is a more refined white-tablecloth experience, but prices are the same. Can be busy on weekend nights, reserve ahead. Absolutely end the meal with the famous

candidates.name: Master Class
candidates.content: Angus beef kebab sandwiches for 1500 drams (Oct 2026), and a few other items on the small, focused menu.

candidates.name: OST
candidates.content: Cheap cafe, lots of food options and drinks. Very central, try the Ajarakan khachapuri or the lahmejun. Free Wi-Fi.

candidates.name: Meghedi
candidates.content: Cheap cafe, lots of food options and drinks. Very central, next to the Opera at the Freedom Square. Free Wi-Fi.

candidates.name: Tumanyan Shaurma
candidates.content: Yerevan style shawarma. A local chain with a dozen restaurants around Yerevan.

candidates.name: Jengyalov Hac
candidates.content: Bakery. Excellent Armenian zhangyalov hats.

candidates.name: Lahmajun Gaidz
candidates.content: Good cheap Armenian fast food, run by a kind and hard working Syrian-Armenian woman.

candidates.name: Vernissage
candidates.content: A walk through the weekend Vernissage open air market through the park between Aram and Buzand Streets is a must. From rugs, souvenirs, instruments and paintings, to pets and chemistry supplies, this outdoor market seemingly has e

candidates.name: Covered Market
candidates.alt: Agricultural bazaar, G.U.M. market, Food Market No. 2
candidates.content: Yerevan's largest food market.

candidates.name: SAS supermarket
candidates.content: A chain. More units: 35 Isahakyan St (16px: Yeritasardakan), 18 Mashtots (16px: Hanrapetutian Hraparak (Republic Square)), 31 Tumanyan (close to Armenian Opera Theater), 85 Baghramyan (16px: Barekamutyun), 20/1 Qajaznuni, 1A Kievy

candidates.name: General Market
candidates.content: A supermarket.

december.text: The Armenian Apostolic Church, or just Apostolic Church, is the National Church of Armenia. It is very traditional; in practices (but not history) is similar to Orthodox and Catholic movements, and to the Reformed Churches, e.g. the Church of England.
